claims.text: Thermal-expansion mismatch during solidification and processing induces residual microstresses in HfNbTaTiZr.
Residual microstresses govern the stress–strain behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Residual microstresses govern the thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Residual microstresses affect behavior by modulating dislocation mobility.
Residual microstresses affect behavior by modulating lattice anharmonicity.
Conventionally processed HfNbTaTiZr inherently contains heterogeneous residual microstresses.
Conventionally processed HfNbTaTiZr contains local lattice distortions caused by thermal-expansion mismatch.
A controlled pre-strain followed by annealing will relax pre-existing thermal residual stresses.
The pre-strain/annealing treatment will reduce local lattice distortions.
Relaxation of residual stress and lattice distortion will make activation of dislocation mechanisms more spatially uniform.
Relaxation of residual stress will stabilize the lattice response.
More uniform dislocation activation and a stabilized lattice response will make macroscopic stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior more predictable and harmonized.
Pre-strained and annealed samples will exhibit fewer elastic-modulus anomalies than as-processed samples.
Pre-strained and annealed samples will exhibit a more consistent tensile-creep response than as-processed samples.
Pre-strained and annealed samples will show thermal expansion closer to theoretical predictions for a uniform microstructure.
As-processed samples retain the original heterogeneous residual-microstress distribution.
The residual-stress effects can be isolated without inducing consequential secondary microstructural changes.
Pre-straining and annealing may also change texture or dislocation density, thereby influencing macroscopic behavior independently of residual-stress relaxation.
